name: Chandrayaan-3
lastSignal: September 2023 — lander and rover did not resume contact after lunar night
tagline: For a brief lunar day, Pragyan traced a path across the Moon and left India with a landing story for the history books.
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Demonstrate safe soft landing, rover mobility and in-situ scientific experiments near the Moon’s south polar region.
beats.achieved: Vikram soft-landed on August 23, 2023. Pragyan deployed and travelled about 101 metres, while instruments on the lander, rover and propulsion module collected scientific data.
beats.ending: The lander and rover were placed into sleep mode before the lunar night, with hopes of waking them after sunrise. Attempts to re-establish communication in September 2023 were unsuccessful.
beats.now: Vikram and Pragyan remain on the lunar surface at the landing region. They are not currently operational; the propulsion module continued in lunar orbit after the lander separation and later performed an Earth-orbit experiment.
beats.learned: Chandrayaan-3 demonstrated India’s soft-landing capability and returned surface measurements of lunar soil, temperature, plasma and seismic activity.
